newsitem.title: USA: US House panel okays airwave auction legislation.
newsitem.headline: US House panel okays airwave auction legislation.

text.p: The House Commerce Committee approved legislation Wednesday that would create minimum bids at federal airwave auctions and allow regulators to void those sales in which bids are considered too low.
The legislation, approved 27-23, is part of an overall bill implementing the fiscal 1998 budget pact agreed to by President Clinton and approved by Congress.
That pact calls for the government to raise $26.3 billion over the next five years through spectrum auctions.
The legislation also would require the Federal Communications Commission to ensure that communications companies have adequate time to prepare for an auction.
The provisions follow a recent FCC auction that fell way short of the $1.87 billion Congress was counting on to help cut the deficit.

The legislation also contained a provision allowing television broadcasters -- in the transition to high-definition digital TV -- to keep their existing analog licenses if five percent of the viewers in their market still use analog sets by the year 2007.
Under current law, the analog licenses are supposed to be auctioned for other uses and broadcasters must then return those licenses to the government following the transition to digital broadcasts.
One other provision would wave existing duopoly and newspaper cross ownership rules for media companies wanting to bid on the analog spectrum in the auction scheduled for 2001.
